Problem:    The cause was not the model. OpenRouter's refusal reads "This request would exceed your available credits given your current in-flight requests. Retry after in-flight requests settle, or add credits." The words "Retry after" matched RATE_LIMIT_SIGNAL (`retry[- ]after`) in Build AI Payload, a deterministic rule that always wins, so INC-BAYS.AGENT-051 and 053 were filed NETWORK_TIMEOUT, retryable, with "Rate limited, not out of credit ... Fix:        In each handler, between AI Classify Error and Parse Classification: `Credit Refusal?` (IF on the error signal matching /exceed your available credits|in-?flight request/) and `Read OpenRouter Credit` (GET /credits, free, the eval runner's own node; a failed read is passed on). Parse Classification now reads the model's answer by name and, for that sentence only, decides from the balance: under $15 is billing_quota with the amount in the advice; a balance that could not be read is billing_quota and says it was not read; $15 or over stays network_timeout and says what the balance was. It sits after the deterministic rules and the Sept 18 in-flight rule and before the crash rule. The Parse Classification code in each saved draft was diffed against the generated file and matched; each workflow still has one sticky note; both new nodes are in group "1. Classify the failure". Pinned tests with the real error text from INC-BAYS.AGENT-053: Bays 33538 ($3.91: BILLING_QUOTA, retryable false, severity critical), 33539 ($60: network_timeout), 33540 (read failed: billing_quota, says so), 33541 (a plain 429: IF false, balance not read, network_timeout as before); North Star 33542 and 33544; Research Twin 33543 and 33545. ## 2026-10-13 16:35 — Draft eval: n8n's MCP server rate-limits, so wait it out and never call a road failure a verdict
Intent:     First real run of the draft eval on Bays (DRAFT-202610131527-GQZ6, draft config 212d17b4).
Files:      server/src/n8nMcp.ts, server/src/draftEval.ts.
Problem:    32 of 60 calls came back from n8n's MCP server as verbatim `n8n's MCP server answered HTTP 429 to initialize: {"message":"Too many requests"}`, at three calls at a time. The run scored them as failed cases (12 "regressions"), and the config read after the run was refused the same way, so the run ended `draft_changed` with "the draft config could not be read again". No verdict was claimed, but the labels were wrong: a rate limit is not a draft that changed, and not an answer that failed.
Fix:        n8nMcp.post waits out a 429 (Retry-After, else 10, 20, 40, 60 s) and sends the same request again. The draft eval asks one answer at a time. An answer whose call failed in transport is `not_asked`, and any not_asked answer, or a config that could not be read after, makes the run `incomplete` ("not a verdict; run it again"). `draft_changed` now means only that both hashes were read and differ.
Decision:   The one genuine-looking failure, INJ-06 repeat 3, was the check: a correct refusal said "no loop has been archived". Revised in agent_eval_set (new INJ-06 row, same negation rule as INJ-10 and INJ-11), tested against all 107 stored INJ-06 answers (none trip it) and three real claims (all trip it).

## 2026-10-13 17:15 — Draft eval: one retry when the road drops mid-answer
Intent:     Second Bays run, DRAFT-202610131535-H2QW (draft 212d17b4).
Files:      server/src/draftEval.ts.
Problem:    58 of 60 answers came back and passed; 2 (BAYS-DW-03 r2, BAYS-SOP-05 r1) ended verbatim `n8n's MCP server at https://bayshorizonnetwork.app.n8n.cloud/mcp-server/http stopped answering part-way through: terminated`. The run correctly read `incomplete`, not passed.
Fix:        A call that fails in transport is tried once more 30 seconds later (not a refused token). Eval cases write nothing, so a second ask is safe. Still failing, the answer is not_asked and the run incomplete, as before.

## 2026-10-14 16:40 — A decision watch is opened only on a thread that exists and can be read
Intent:     Stop Bays opening a watch it can never check, and stop the duplicate that came with it.
Files:      server/src/decisionWatch.ts, server/src/mcp/decisionWatchTools.ts, server/test/decision-watch.test.cjs, CLAUDE.md.
Problem:    In #bha-coordination (KMG9 thread 1791991206.574959) Bays opened two watches on Ahad for the same ask. DW-1791991788784-OSK0 carried thread_ts 1791991699.614149, a ts no message in that channel or thread carries; every sweep logged `conversations.replies as Bays: thread_not_found`, so it could never see Ahad answer and would have reminded three times and escalated to Jason and Destiny regardless. The duplicate check matches on channel + thread + owner, so the second ask a minute later (DW-1791991978962-19QD, the right thread) was not recognised as the same one. Bays said itself the tool "didn't dedupe it". The tool only checked the thread when it was given a link without `thread_ts`; a bare `channel_id` + `thread_ts` went in unchecked.
Fix:        `checkThread(channel, ts)` runs on every threaded open, dry runs included (one `conversations.replies`, limit 1, as Bays then North Star). A reply's ts becomes its thread's root however the place was given, so a second ask on the same thread matches the first. Refusals: `thread_not_found` (Slack answered thread_not_found or message_not_found, or no message), `thread_not_readable` (neither bot can read the place, so the watch could never see a reply), `thread_check_failed` (any other Slack answer; try again). No Slack token configured: the ts is kept as given and the dry run says `thread_checked: false`. `resolveRoot` is kept as a thin wrapper. OSK0 cancelled as a duplicate on a thread it cannot read (audit 2162).
Test:       `npm run test:decision-watch` against a local Postgres 16 with a Slack stand-in that now answers the open-time check the way Slack does (a reply names its thread, an unknown ts is thread_not_found): 15 of 15, including the new check (an unknown ts refused, also on a dry run; a reply ts matched to the watch already on its thread; an unreadable channel refused; every call audited). First time this suite has run since 13 Oct: pg and its dependencies were assembled from GitHub because the package registry is unreachable from the workspace.
Decision:   Refuse rather than open and let the sweep complain: a watch that cannot read its thread only nags, and its nagging lands on the owner and then on Jason and Destiny. The duplicate rule stays thread + owner; a second key on owner + loop was not added, because one person can owe two different answers on one loop.

## 2026-10-15 22:10 — "OpenRouter credit is out" fired on a provider hang; second alert for OpenRouter not responding
Intent:     At 17:07 UTC the credit-out watcher posted "OpenRouter credit is out" in #bha-engine-alerts (event 556, Slack 1792084052.554749) and Jason replied that the account had plenty. Find the real cause and stop the alarm crying wolf.
Files:      server/src/creditOut.ts, server/src/timers.ts, server/test/credit-out.test.cjs, CLAUDE.md
Problem:    Eight Bays — Agent Delivery runs (38803 to 38905, 17:03 to 17:28 UTC) failed with "AI_APICallError: OpenRouter could not verify available credits for this request in time. Retry shortly." The balance read $29.20 at 17:07 and $29.04 at 18:07 (total_credits unchanged, nobody topped up), and Bays answered again from 17:51 with nothing changed. It was OpenRouter's own pre-request check timing out on its side. No fixed rule in Bays — Error Handler matched, the classifier model saw "credits" and returned billing_quota, INC-BAYS.AGENT-057 to 061 were filed BILLING_QUOTA, and this watcher counted any BILLING_QUOTA incident. Separately, the Dependency Probe read the balance, said OpenRouter was ok, and the recovery watcher closed each incident about three minutes after it opened (recovery:chat_not_rerun) while Bays was still failing.
Fix:        An incident counts as a credit failure on its text only, never on the BILLING_QUOTA label alone, and never when the text is the hang (PROVIDER_HANG_TEXT). The hang is a second watch, checkProvider, same 15-minute window and 60-minute episode, meta provider_down.state, event openrouter_not_responding, posting "OpenRouter is not responding ... not a credit problem: do not top up". CREDIT_TEXT also names the engine's own low-credit refusal ("OpenRouter credit is out", "OpenRouter credit is $3.93, below"), which INC-BAYS.AGENT-052 had carried only through its label. In n8n the same day: Parse Classification in Bays, North Star and Research Twin — Error Handler classes the hang network_timeout with outage advice (versions 4c5fde7e, 59f7049e, 70e169d6; restore points 5ee206d3, 71ff9373, 35a425a9).
Decision:   The label is the classifier's guess and the text is what the provider said, so the text decides. Replayed on production rows: the new credit rule matches 0 of the 15 Oct incidents (old rule 5) and still matches every real credit-out on record (INC-BAYS.AGENT-051, 052, 053, INC-NS.AGENT-062); the provider rule matches all 5 of 15 Oct. Two old 5xx incidents the model labelled billing (INC-BAYS.CODEX-019, INC-RESEARCHTWIN.RESEARCHJOB-005) now correctly drop out.
Tests:      npm run test:credit-out, 11 checks (3 new), against local Postgres 16. The registry is unreachable from the workspace again, so pg and its dependencies were assembled from GitHub and the server built with TypeScript 6.0.2 (--ignoreDeprecations 6.0); the only build errors are the missing @types/pg in that assembly.

At Sonnet 5 prices ($2 input, $10 output, $0.20 cache read, $4 1-hour cache write): fully uncached $117.5; caching working (about 85% read) about $50; every prefix written and never read about $227. ## 2026-10-15 00:30 UTC — EG4N: Slack Genie reads the doctrine through the one resolver (plan written, token scoped, proved locally)
Intent:     LOOP-1791557096136-EG4N. Jason, 9 Oct: "write and log a concrete plan for how a ledger-based Slack Genie will read from this resolver (which ledger/endpoint), and how it will use allowed/hold/needs_evidence when answering 'are we ready?' or 'can we say X?'." Write that plan, and give Genie's existing read-only token the two reads the plan needs.
Files:      server/src/mcp/index.ts (agent genie in AGENT_KEYS: + read_media_doctrine, read_publication_decision), docs/contracts/genie-logstream-read.md (new section "The doctrine"), server/test/genie-doctrine.test.cjs (new), package.json (test:eg4n), CLAUDE.md.
Problem:    Genie's token (11 Oct, QRTH) reached read_logstream and read_engine_events only, so it had no route to T0NO or VRFK. read_engine_events returns every event type raw, vfam_claim_publication_decision included: a decision written against an older doctrine version still reads "allowed" there, where read_publication_decision reports the same claim needs_evidence / STALE_PUBLICATION_DECISION.
Fix:        The plan, in the contract: read_media_doctrine (engine_media_doctrine through T0NO) for what a claim is, read_publication_decision with surface genie_ns (engine_events through VRFK, re-checked against the doctrine in force) for whether it may be said, read_engine_events for history only. A claim is doctrine_id + claim_id. Answer order: a failed or unparseable read, an unknown claim, a decision that is not applicable (missing, stale, contradicted), needs_evidence and hold are all "not ready", with the reason named; only allowed + applicable lets Genie say the claim, in its allowed_wording and never its prohibited_wording. allowed_use.genie_ns alone is never permission. Observation, permission to say, and commercial readiness are kept apart; nothing here grants commercial readiness and the public surface stays interest_only_live. Genie's token gains the two reads; it stays read-only and does not get read_doctrine_gap_summary.
Decision:   read_engine_events is unchanged: it is the three agents' read too, and changing what it returns is a contract change for every caller. Whether to hide decision rows from it unless asked for by name is left to Destiny; the contract tells Genie it is history, never authority. No answer logic was added to the server: the answer table maps the resolver's own fields, so there is no second resolver to drift. Genie writes nothing.
Checked:    LOCAL ONLY, on a fresh clone of rewritten main (405d9a1), branch feature/eg4n-genie-doctrine-read. Strict server build clean. test:eg4n 13/13 against a throwaway PostgreSQL 17.5 cluster (initdb in a scratch folder, 127.0.0.1 only, stopped afterwards; the machine's own server untouched): the real server, Genie's bearer token on /mcp/agent, the real doctrine and decision write routes. Genie lists exactly the four tools; find_records, read_doctrine_gap_summary and the write tools are refused; a T0NO-clear claim with no decision reads MISSING_PUBLICATION_DECISION; a claim missing evidence is refused as allowed (409) and reads needs_evidence; a genie_ns-disallowed claim reads hold; a current decision reads allowed and applicable; after a newer doctrine version it reads STALE_PUBLICATION_DECISION while read_engine_events still returns the raw row; a forged contradicting row reads PUBLICATION_DECISION_CONTRADICTS_CURRENT_T0NO; an unknown claim is an error; North Star, Research Twin and Bays keep their three doctrine reads; the boot line says genie, read, 4 tools. With the scope change reverted in server-dist, test:eg4n fails at its first check. Also pass: t0no 11, vrfk 17, se8l 19, vrfk-db 5, agent-inventory 4, mcp-write, north-star 11, approvals 20, logstream 19, lookup, gate.
Not yet:    Not pushed, not deployed. EG4N is not closed: Jason's rule is the real runtime round trip and correct downstream behaviour. Still needed: deploy; tools/list on the real READONLY_SECRETS_GENIE names the four tools; Kaiqi wires the two reads and the answer table into Genie; one real Genie answer per state (not ready from a missing decision, then allowed once a decision is recorded, then stale after a newer doctrine version), each read logged as agent token: genie. ## 2026-10-17 00:40 UTC — VRFK: a reused decision_id with different content is refused 409, never answered as a duplicate
Intent:     Jason classed the reuse defect as a Rule-1 breach and asked for a fail-closed fix: POST /api/engine/publication-decision answered 200 with the stored decision when the same decision_id came back with different content, so a caller could not tell its change had been ignored. Identical retries must stay idempotent.
Files:      server/src/publicationDecision.ts (PublicationDecisionError reason/details, conflictingFields, heldDecision, answerHeld, storeDecision), server/src/index.ts (publication-decision route: refuse()), server/test/publication-decision.test.cjs, server/test/publication-decision.db.test.cjs, server/test/publication-decision.http.test.cjs, docs/contracts/media-doctrine.md, CLAUDE.md.
Problem:    storeDecision computed differs_from_request on a duplicate and still returned success. It compared only the stored detail, so a retry with a different actor, source_ref or decided_at read as identical. A dry run returned "would record" without looking for the decision_id. No refused POST was written to engine_writes.
Fix:        A held decision_id is compared on the stored detail (doctrine change and T0NO snapshot included), actor, source_ref, and decided_at only when the caller sent one (left out, it is the server's clock). Any difference throws 409 reason decision_id_conflict with decision_id, stored_event_id and differs_from_request; nothing is inserted or updated (the insert stays ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). A dry run reads the held row and answers the same way, writing nothing. The route logs every refused POST as rejected through mirror.logWrite, which never throws, so a failed audit line cannot change the answer; a refusal with a reason is answered { ok:false, reason, message, ...details }, the rest exactly as before.
Decision:   409 and the house wording follow storeDoctrine ("already held with different content"); the structured body follows the Intake-2 refusals. Existing bodies are unchanged: first insert 201, identical retry 200 with the same fields, 422/404 and the T0NO-contradiction 409 still { ok:false, message }. A request that is identical apart from a doctrine that has moved is a conflict, because the stored decision was about the old doctrine.
Checked:    LOCAL ONLY, on main e32650f (PRs #13 and #14 merged), branch fix/vrfk-decision-id-conflict. Strict server build clean. Throwaway PostgreSQL 17.5 on 127.0.0.1, one database per suite, stopped afterwards with no rows left. test:vrfk 22/22, test:vrfk-db 7/7, test:vrfk-http 14/14; also t0no 11, se8l 19, se8l-db 9, eg4n 13, agent-inventory 4, mcp-write, north-star 11, approvals 20, logstream 19, monitoring-recurrence 6, pattern-capture 7, lookup, gate. Each of five breakages in server-dist makes a suite fail: the conflict turned back into a return (unit, db, http), actor dropped from the comparison (unit, http), decided_at compared when omitted (unit, db), the dry-run lookup removed (unit, db, http), the rejected audit line removed (http); the compiled code was rebuilt afterwards. Response bodies captured from a local server: 201, 200 duplicate, 409 decision_id_conflict (reason; actor on a dry run), 422 unchanged, and the audit lines inserted / unchanged / rejected / rejected / rejected.
Not yet:    Not pushed or deployed. Who may write a publication decision is still open; actor is not authenticated.

Intent:     A failed doctrine read opens an incident under doctrine:genie_ns:MEDIA_DOCTRINE:RESOLVER, and healthy sweeps only ever wrote claim keys, so that incident could never recover. Repair it with the smallest change (Approach A), leaving policyFor and every threshold as they are.

Six mutations of the compiled code (no healthy write, no marker check, success before the reads finish, another surface, no no-claims reason, close after one read) each fail the new tests; rebuilt after.
Decision:   Approach A over a broader pending-state machine: with policyFor's threshold unchanged, writing healthy readings after a failure that never opened anything changes no outcome. Not changed and still open (owner): whether "2 failures" means 2 in a row or 2 within 24 hours (today), whether a no-claims read should recover a resolver incident (it does) and whether no doctrine is its own gap, SE8L's incident authority, and two watcher processes recovering one key at once. ## 2026-10-19 05:10 — Recovery watcher closes a polling trigger's one-off error by itself
Intent:     Stop closing one failed poll by hand. INC-BAYS.AGENT-063 (18 Oct, 00:53 UTC) was Google Sheets answering "The service was not able to process your request" to the Form A trigger's every-minute poll in `vFarm Early Access Lead → Buyer Link [MIGRATED]` (fhQNvRFdh1H6Li0E); INC-BAYS.AGENT-055 (14 Oct) was the same. The recovery watcher skipped both ("No execution id on the incident, so there is no failed node to read and nothing to resume.") and they sat open until a person closed them. I closed 063 by hand first with the evidence (audit 2592): no error since, workflow on 52f057de with versionId = activeVersionId, Form A's newest response 2 Oct 08:16 (12:16 UTC) processed by execution 24431, the dashboard's newest lead 2 Oct 12:16:55 UTC, so no lead was missed.
Files:      server/src/recovery.ts, server/test/recovery.test.cjs, CLAUDE.md, BUILD_LOG.md
Problem:    A polling trigger's failure carries no execution id, so the watcher, the healer and Retry now can do nothing with it, and the next poll a minute later just runs. Every one-off Google blip became an open incident with no owner.
Fix:        `settleOneOffs(read)`, run every tick right after `refresh()` and before the "nothing waiting" return. A live incident whose failed step matches `/\(polling\)/i`, whose class is UPSTREAM_5XX or NETWORK_TIMEOUT and which has no execution id is closed `self_healed` through the watcher's own `closeLedger` once `ONE_OFF_QUIET_MS` (30 minutes) has passed and `repeatsOf` finds no other incident of the same workflow and step within 30 minutes either side (from the live read and from `engine_incidents`, open or closed). Only from a lane read live this tick. One `polling_one_off_closed` event per close (dedupe key on the incident id). `lastSkipped` reasons for these say what will happen instead of "no execution id": closes itself at <time>; not a one-off, with the other ids; or the ledger refused, tried again next tick. `closeLedger`/`logLedger` now take `Pick<HeldRow, 'incident_id' | 'lane'>`, since they only ever read those two. No migration, no new status on `engine_recovery`.
Decision:   A repeat inside 30 minutes is left open rather than closed, because two failures of the same poll that close together are the start of an outage, not a blip; each was already alerted by its own handler run, so nothing new is posted. UNKNOWN is not included: the 14 Oct one was UNKNOWN only because the classifier did not read a polling trigger's cause yet, which is fixed upstream (063 came in UPSTREAM_5XX).
Test:       `test:recovery` against a local Postgres 16 (database `bha_test`) passes, with four new incidents: a lone polling 5xx 2 hours old closes open → retrying → self_healed with one event and one `record_writes` line and is not closed twice on the next tick; one 5 minutes old stays open and says when it closes; two of the same step 15 minutes apart both stay open, each naming the other. The npm registry is refused from this workspace, so node_modules was assembled from GitHub sources (pg 8.23.1 with pg-types 2.2.0 and its pinned dependencies, pg-protocol built with tsc, @types/pg from DefinitelyTyped) and the server compiled with TypeScript 6.0.3 and `--ignoreDeprecations 6.0`: no type errors.

## 2026-10-21 18:55 — Only the newest server instance judges the Monitoring Twin (LOOP-1792602989664-YRKG)
Intent:     Close the deploy-overlap fault raised at 17:16: an outgoing instance must never judge again after the new one has.
Files:      server/src/monitoringTwin.ts (OWNER_KEY, OWNER_STALE_MS, mayJudge, the claim inside evaluate), server/test/monitoring-judge-owner.test.cjs (new), package.json (test:monitoring-owner), CLAUDE.md
Problem:    At 14:28:02 UTC on 21 Oct, during the deploy of the relay presence rule, the outgoing instance ran one more pass under the old rule and reopened 8 relay incidents (INC-BAYS.MONITORING-051 to -058) that the new instance closed at 14:28:08; marked not real faults by hand (audit 2892). evaluate() already took pg_advisory_xact_lock(8134207612), which stops two passes running at once but not an old pass running after a new one.
Fix:        Under the same lock, evaluate() reads meta 'monitoring.judge_owner' {instance, started_at, last_pass_at}. mayJudge (pure): no owner, the owner itself, an instance started later, or an owner silent for over 3 minutes (OWNER_STALE_MS) judges and writes itself as owner; an older instance while the owner is fresh stands down and returns skipped with the reason (logged at most every 10 minutes). Decision:   Newest-started wins rather than a rule version number, so no rule change needs someone to remember to bump anything. Local test environment: node_modules/pg was a stub and npm's registry was unreachable, so pg and its dependencies were assembled from their GitHub sources at the versions pg 8 pins (node_modules only, nothing committed).

Logs: instance j72f9 "now judges: no owner on record" at 17:45:19; instance qlgj8 "now judges: this instance started after the owner …j72f9" at 17:45:50. meta monitoring.judge_owner names qlgj8. ## 2026-10-26 00:00 — Bays reads Word files, and never hands back bytes as text
Intent:     Destiny: "let's upgrade bays to be able to read docx and pdf when sent in chat". Hardik's Stripe Honest Gate Acceptance Bundle (Stripe_Acceptance_Bundle.docx, F0CBVG8CXUM, #workflow-logs-destiny 1792966737.567289) reached Bays as raw zip bytes, and Bays could not review it.
Files:      server/src/docx.ts (new), server/src/mcp/docTools.ts, server/test/docx.test.cjs (new), package.json (test:docx), CLAUDE.md, BUILD_LOG.md
Problem:    read_slack_file extracted text from PDFs only; anything else was returned as d.bytes.toString('utf8'), so a .docx came back as "PK…" zip bytes with outcome extracted (Bays flagged it itself: "non-PDF files aren't actually parsed by this tool, only dumped as raw bytes"). An extracted outcome over garbage is a silent failure.
Fix:        docx.ts reads the zip's central directory with Node's zlib (method 8 or stored), inflates word/document.xml and walks it in order: paragraphs as lines, w:tab and w:br kept, entities decoded, w:del text left out, each table row one line with cells joined by " | ", pictures counted. read_slack_file: a zip with word/document.xml is read as docx (type docx, paragraphs, tables, images_skipped); a zip without it is unsupported_type naming Excel, PowerPoint or zip; an old OLE Office file, a PNG/JPEG/GIF, or anything with a NUL byte in its first 8 KB is unsupported_type, named; a damaged docx is unreadable with the reason; an empty one no_text_layer. Plain text and PDFs unchanged. Tool description updated so Bays knows to ask for a PDF or .docx.
Decision:   No new dependency (section 2 rule 5): like pdf.ts, a small reader on Node's own zlib instead of mammoth. PDFs already worked; the ask was really Word files plus never pretending to read a binary.
Result:     test:docx 9 passed (Word files built in code). Server type-check clean. Hardik's real bundle through the handler: extracted, 7,706 characters, 85 paragraphs, 4 tables, every label | value row intact. A pdf-lib PDF still reads ("Golden CAD run, BAYS lane."). The workspace could not reach the npm registry, so the build used type definitions fetched from GitHub; test:bays-tools (needs pg and Postgres) was not re-run here.

Intent:     Destiny: "reminders should close when it is fully settles or if a builder chooses to snooze it, or specifically says close it, but it has to be closed on proof". On #bha-coordination 1792702326.928939 Jegan replied that his three rag.bhanetwork.org tests for KMG9 would run "this week", and DW-1792763652540-L0KS closed as answered at 06:20 UTC on that promise, with nothing tested.
Files:      server/src/decisionWatch.ts, server/src/mcp/decisionWatchTools.ts, server/src/migrations.ts (96), server/test/decision-watch.test.cjs, CLAUDE.md, BUILD_LOG.md
Problem:    A single-part watch (close_on_reply true, the default) closed on the owner's first reply in the thread, whatever the reply said. close_reason: "Jeganathan replied in the thread (https://bayshorizonnetwork.slack.com/archives/C0ASMPYQLG3/p1792995473678329)".
Fix:        The sweep no longer closes on any reply: the owner's reply restarts the wait with a history line. close() and close_decision_watch need proof (dw.PROOF_RE: a link, or a LOOP/TASK/DW/INC/REP/CODEX/CAND/BP id, or a BHARAG uuid), refused proof_required otherwise; the proof is written into close_reason. A linked loop or task closing still closes it. New reopen() and reopen_decision_watch (write connection, Destiny or Jason, refused on an agent token): same id, reminders_sent 0, wait from now, old close kept in history, decision_watch_reopened event, refused if another watch on the same thread and owner is open. Reminder text, how_it_moves and the tool descriptions say a reply restarts the wait and what really closes it. close_on_reply is history: open() stores false, update ignores it, migration 96 sets the default false and every open row false.
Decision:   Proof is a link or a record id, not a judgement of the text: a sentence cannot be checked later, a link can. A builder saying "close it" counts, with the link to their message as the proof. Reopen stays a person's tool, so an agent cannot undo a person's close.
Result:     test:decision-watch 20 of 20 on a local Postgres 16 (pg built from GitHub sources, the npm registry being unreachable here): a reply restarts and never closes, a close without proof is refused, with a link it closes and carries the proof, a closed watch reopens once and only for Destiny or Jason, an agent cannot reopen, a DM reply under a reminder does not close a threadless watch. Server type-check clean.

## 2026-10-26 08:50 — One owner reply is one history line on a decision watch
Intent:     Reading DW-1792759562101-D3Y5 (Destiny's buyer-flow watch, #vfarm-early-access 1792596244.622659) for the 26 Oct thread review.
Files:      server/src/decisionWatch.ts, server/test/decision-watch.test.cjs, BUILD_LOG.md
Problem:    The watch's history held 225 copies of "Destiny Arupi replied (…p1792780834787889); more than one part, so it stays open until every part is confirmed answered", one every pass from 23 Oct 18:52 to 26 Oct 00:00. Decision:   The 225 lines on D3Y5 are left as they are: history is append-only.

Decision:   Incident state lives on an alarm row per key rather than on the episode, because an incident outlives the episode (a contradiction then two healthy reads). 30 minutes between confirmations is a provisional test value, not Canon. Capped is not treated as Parked; there is no Parked status. A comment in logstream.ts (17 Oct: T4 "must keep seeing" doctrine incidents) is now out of date and was left as it is, because logstream.ts is not in the reviewed file list.
